q:
After upgrading to OPA 1.21, a policy fails to load:

```text
rego_parse_error: `if` keyword is required before rule body
rego_parse_error: `contains` keyword is required for partial set rules
```

The rule reads `deny[msg] { input.kind == "Deployment"; ... }`. What is the permanent fix?
options: Add `import future.keywords` at the top of the file
Rewrite the rule in Rego v1: `deny contains msg if { ... }`
explain: OPA 1.x requires Rego v1 syntax by default, where multi-value rules have `contains` and the body has `if`. `--v0-compatible` is only a temporary workaround; imports and renaming don't change the rule syntax.

q: The policies are in `policy/k8s.rego` with `package kubernetes`. `conftest test k8s/deployment.yaml` reports no FAIL even though the container is privileged. What is the cause?
options: Conftest evaluates the `main` package by default; you need `--namespace kubernetes` or `--all-namespaces`
The YAML file needs an explicit `--parser yaml`
Policies must be in the `policies/` directory
You need `--combine` for Conftest to see all containers
explain: Conftest looks for rules in the `main` package unless you specify another namespace. The parser is chosen by extension, the default directory is `policy/`, and `--combine` merges several files into one input.

q: The `warn_limits` rule reports containers without a memory limit, but the pipeline stays green. The team wants warnings to break the build without changing the policies. Which flag?
explain: With `--fail-on-warn` Conftest returns exit 1 for warnings (and 2 for failures). The other flags change package selection, input shape or output format, but not the exit code.

q: The `node-exporter` DaemonSet legitimately needs `hostPath`. All other rules (privileges, registries, tag) must still apply to it. Which Conftest exception is correct?
options: `exception contains rules if { input.kind == "DaemonSet"; input.metadata.name == "node-exporter"; rules := ["hostpath"] }`
explain: `rules` contains rule suffixes, so `"hostpath"` disables only `deny_hostpath`/`violation_hostpath` for that DaemonSet. An empty string disables all rules named `deny`, the full name `deny_hostpath` doesn't match as a suffix, and Conftest doesn't use `allow_` rules for exceptions.

q: The list of allowed registries changes every month, and the `deny_registry` policy is the same across 30 repos. How should this be organized?
options: The list in `data/registries.yaml` (`allowed_registries: [...]`), the policy reads `data.allowed_registries`, and Conftest runs with `--data data`
Hardcode the list into every copy of the policy
Create a separate policy for each registry
Pass the list through a CI variable and read it with an `opa.runtime()` call in every rule
explain: `--data` loads JSON/YAML data available as `data.*`, so the list changes without touching the Rego. Hardcoding and separate policies multiply the changes, and environment variables are not the intended mechanism for policy data.

q:
A rule is supposed to require `runAsNonRoot`:

```rego
deny_root contains msg if {
	some c in containers
	c.securityContext.runAsNonRoot == false
	msg := sprintf("%s runs as root", [c.name])
}
```

A Deployment without any `securityContext` passes. Why?
options: Conftest has a bug with non-existent fields; you need `--strict`
A non-existent field is undefined, so the comparison is not true and the rule doesn't hold; you need `not c.securityContext.runAsNonRoot`
explain: In Rego an expression over a non-existent field is neither true nor an error, so the rule body doesn't succeed. `not c.securityContext.runAsNonRoot` is true both when the field is missing and when it is `false`. This is language behavior, not a Conftest bug.

q: Someone changed `deny_privileged` and accidentally disabled it completely. The pipeline stayed green and a privileged Deployment got through. What should have been in the job before `conftest test`?
options: `conftest verify --policy policy` with tests such as `test_privileged_denied`
explain: `conftest verify` runs Rego unit tests (`test_*`); a test expecting a FAIL for a privileged container would have failed and stopped the pipeline. Formatting, a different output or a manual `opa eval` don't check that the policy still works.

q: After upgrading the Kyverno CLI to 1.19, `kyverno apply` prints a warning about your `ClusterPolicy` files alongside the results. What is the correct conclusion?
options: The CLI no longer supports ClusterPolicy and the results are invalid
You should switch to OPA Gatekeeper
`ClusterPolicy` is deprecated in 1.19 with removal announced for 1.20; write new policies as `ValidatingPolicy` (CEL) and plan the migration
explain: In 1.19 ClusterPolicy still works but is deprecated, and the CEL types (`ValidatingPolicy`, `ImageValidatingPolicy`...) are the recommended path. `validationFailureAction` itself has been replaced by `failureAction` in the rule.

q: A `ValidatingPolicy` has the expression `object.spec.template.spec.containers.all(c, c.securityContext.privileged == false)`. For a Deployment whose container has no `securityContext`, evaluation reports an error instead of a result. What is the fix?
options: Guard optional fields with `has()`: `!has(c.securityContext) || !has(c.securityContext.privileged) || c.securityContext.privileged == false`
explain: In CEL, accessing a non-existent field is an error, so optional fields must be checked with `has()`. Audit, `matchConditions` and `failurePolicy` change what happens with the result or the error, but they don't fix the expression.

q: You are writing `kyverno-test.yaml` for the `ValidatingPolicy` `kurs-deployment-baseline`. What must every entry in `results` contain, besides `policy`, `kind`, `resources` and `result`?
options: `kind: ValidatingPolicy` instead of the resource kind
explain: For a Kyverno CEL `ValidatingPolicy` the result is marked with `isValidatingPolicy: true` and there are no named rules. `isValidatingAdmissionPolicy` is for Kubernetes VAP, and `kind` is the kind of the tested resource (Deployment).

q: You are introducing a new Kyverno policy. For the first two weeks the cluster should only record violations, and the pipeline should show them as warnings, not as a failure. Which combination?
options: `validationActions: [Deny]` in the cluster and `kyverno apply --audit-warn` in CI
`validationActions: [Audit]` in the cluster and `kyverno apply --audit-warn` in CI
`validationActions: [Audit]` in the cluster and `kyverno apply --policy-report` in CI
`validationActions: [Deny]` in the cluster and `kyverno apply --continue-on-fail` in CI
explain: Audit in the cluster records violations in a policy report without rejecting, and `--audit-warn` in the CLI shows violations of Audit policies as warnings. Deny would block deploys immediately, `--policy-report` only changes the output format, and `--continue-on-fail` doesn't change the outcome.

q: The same rule ("no public resources") must be checked against a Terraform plan, a Dockerfile and `.gitlab-ci.yml`, with one language and in CI. Which tool?
explain: Conftest parses many formats (JSON plan, Dockerfile, YAML) and evaluates them with Rego policies in CI. Kyverno and Gatekeeper are primarily for Kubernetes resources at admission, and `ImageValidatingPolicy` verifies image signatures.

q: A Conftest policy checks `tfplan.json` (the output of `terraform show -json`). Which path in `input` leads to the planned value of `publicly_accessible` for an `aws_db_instance`?
explain: The JSON plan has `resource_changes`, and the planned state of a resource is in `change.after`. The second option matches the HCL source, the third Trivy's internal cloud model, and the fourth a Kubernetes manifest.

q: The Conftest gate in the pipeline works, but someone ran a privileged Deployment in production with `kubectl apply` from a laptop. Which control prevents this?
options: Kyverno (or Gatekeeper) admission in the cluster with the same policy
A protected branch on the main branch
explain: An admission controller checks every request to the API server, regardless of where it comes from. Pre-commit, protected branches and a stricter CI gate only protect the path through the repo and the pipeline.

q: An application team deleted `deny_hostpath` from `policy/k8s.rego` in their own repo because it bothered them, and the pipeline passed. How do you prevent this?
options: Keep policies in a central repo included at a pinned version (`include: project`, `ref`), and allow only exceptions in the application repo, with CODEOWNERS approval from the security team
Set `allow_failure: false` on the policy job
explain: When policies live in a central repo, the team can't change them with a single commit, and exceptions go through review. `.gitignore`, `--all-namespaces` and `allow_failure` don't prevent a rule from being deleted.

q: Order the steps for introducing a new Conftest rule in an organization with many repos.
options: Rename the rule to `deny_...` and turn on the gate
Write the rule as `warn_...` with tests (`test_*`)
In CI run `conftest verify`, then `conftest test`
Track how many repos are affected and send the teams fix instructions
explain: The rule first comes in as a warning with tests, CI verifies and applies it, the teams get time and instructions, and only then does the warning become a gate.

q: Match each Conftest rule with its behavior.
targets: A unit test run by `conftest verify` or `opa test`
Disables rules by suffix for specific inputs
explain: `deny_` produces a FAIL, `warn_` a warning, `exception` disables rules by suffix, and `test_` rules are unit tests. Modifying resources is done by a Kyverno `MutatingPolicy`, not Conftest.

q: You are migrating the old policy `deny[msg] { input.kind == "Pod"; msg := "..." }` to OPA 1.21 without a compatibility mode. Which TWO changes are required? (Choose TWO.)
options: Add `contains` for a rule that builds a set of messages
explain: Rego v1 requires `contains` for multi-value rules and `if` before the body: `deny contains msg if { ... }`. `import rego.v1` isn't needed in OPA 1.x, and the package name and `result.new` (a Trivy function) have nothing to do with the syntax.
